title: Length: Converting mm, cm, m and km with Decimals
seo_title: Grade 6 Length Worksheets with Answers (CAPS Maths)
standard_text: Estimate, measure, record, compare and order lengths using appropriate measuring instruments; use millimetres (mm), centimetres (cm), metres (m) and kilometres (km); calculate and solve problems involving length, including problems with decimal fractions to 2 decimal places; convert between mm, cm, m and km, including conversions with decimal fractions.
meta_desc: Free CAPS Grade 6 length worksheets: choosing units, converting mm, cm, m and km with decimals, comparing lengths and problems. 100 questions with memos.
key_big: Smaller unit: multiply. Bigger unit: divide.
body_html:
How to think about it

  • 10 mm = 1 cm, 100 cm = 1 m, 1 000 m = 1 km.
  • To change to a smaller unit, multiply: 2,5 m = 250 cm.
  • To change to a bigger unit, divide: 1 750 m = 1,75 km.
  • Change to the same unit before you compare, add or subtract.

Examples

Example

3,2 km − 850 m

3,2 km = 3 200 m

3 200 − 850

Answer: 2 350 m

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
100 m in a km1 km = 1 000 m.
The comma the wrong wayA bigger unit gives a smaller number.
Different unitsChange to the same unit first.

items.q: Which is the most sensible measurement for the length of a classroom?
items.e: A classroom is about 10 big steps long, so 9,5 m fits. 9,5 cm is only the width of a hand, and 95 m is longer than a whole row of classrooms.

items.q: Which is the most sensible measurement for the thickness of a mobile phone?
items.e: A phone is thinner than 1 cm, so use millimetres. 8 cm is as thick as a large book.

items.q: A carpenter measures a board as 2 m 45 cm. How is this written in metres?
Ofentse jumps 312 cm in the long jump. Which shows this in metres?
items.e: 1 m = 100 cm, so divide by 100: 312 ÷ 100 = 3,12 m. The digits move 2 places to the right.

items.q: An ant is 0,006 m long. Which shows the same length in a more sensible unit?
items.e: 1 m = 1 000 mm, so 0,006 × 1 000 = 6 mm. A small number of millimetres is easier to read than a decimal with zeros.

items.q: A road is 0,004 km wide. Which shows the same width in a more sensible unit?
items.e: 1 km = 1 000 m, so 0,004 × 1 000 = 4 m. Metres suit the width of a road.

items.q: A cricket oval is 1 km 60 m around the outside. Which shows this in kilometres?
items.e: 60 m = 60 ÷ 1 000 = 0,06 km. So 1 km 60 m = 1,06 km. 1,6 km would be 1 km 600 m.

items.q: Which is the best estimate for the length of a soccer field?
items.e: A soccer field is about 100 m.

items.q: Which is the best estimate for the length of the road from Cape Town to Stellenbosch?

items.q: Convert. 45 mm = ☐ cm
items.e: 1 cm = 10 mm. Millimetres are smaller than centimetres, so divide by 10: 45 ÷ 10 = 4,5. The digits move 1 place to the right. So 45 mm = 4,5 cm.

items.q: Convert. 3,6 m = ☐ cm
items.e: 1 m = 100 cm. Metres are bigger than centimetres, so multiply by 100: 3,6 × 100 = 360. The digits move 2 places to the left. So 3,6 m = 360 cm.

items.q: Convert. 2,4 km = ☐ m
items.e: 1 km = 1 000 m. Kilometres are bigger than metres, so multiply by 1 000: 2,4 × 1 000 = 2 400. The digits move 3 places to the left. So 2,4 km = 2 400 m.

items.q: Convert. 850 m = ☐ km
items.e: 1 km = 1 000 m. Metres are smaller than kilometres, so divide by 1 000: 850 ÷ 1 000 = 0,85. The digits move 3 places to the right. So 850 m = 0,85 km.

items.q: Convert. 0,6 cm = ☐ mm
items.e: 1 cm = 10 mm. Centimetres are bigger than millimetres, so multiply by 10: 0,6 × 10 = 6. The digits move 1 place to the left. So 0,6 cm = 6 mm.

items.q: Convert. 1,75 m = ☐ mm
items.e: 1 m = 1 000 mm. Metres are bigger than millimetres, so multiply by 1 000: 1,75 × 1 000 = 1 750. The digits move 3 places to the left. So 1,75 m = 1 750 mm. (1,75 × 100 = 175 would give centimetres, not millimetres.)

items.q: Convert. 45 mm = ☐ m
items.e: 1 m = 1 000 mm. Millimetres are smaller than metres, so divide by 1 000: 45 ÷ 1 000 = 0,045. The digits move 3 places to the right, so you need a 0 in the tenths place. So 45 mm = 0,045 m.

items.q: Convert. 3,125 km = ☐ m
items.e: 1 km = 1 000 m. Kilometres are bigger than metres, so multiply by 1 000: 3,125 × 1 000 = 3 125. The digits move 3 places to the left. So 3,125 km = 3 125 m.

items.q: Convert. 65 m = ☐ km
items.e: 1 km = 1 000 m. Metres are smaller than kilometres, so divide by 1 000: 65 ÷ 1 000 = 0,065. The digits move 3 places to the right. So 65 m = 0,065 km. Check: 0,65 km would be 650 m.

items.q: Convert. 7 cm = ☐ m
items.e: 1 m = 100 cm. Centimetres are smaller than metres, so divide by 100: 7 ÷ 100 = 0,07. The digits move 2 places to the right. So 7 cm = 0,07 m.

items.q: Convert. 1,25 m = ☐ cm
items.e: 1 m = 100 cm. Metres are bigger than centimetres, so multiply by 100: 1,25 × 100 = 125. The digits move 2 places to the left. So 1,25 m = 125 cm.

items.q: Convert. 1,5 m = ☐ cm
items.e: 1 m = 100 cm. Metres are bigger than centimetres, so multiply by 100: 1,5 × 100 = 150. The digits move 2 places to the left. So 1,5 m = 150 cm. (1,5 m is 1 m 50 cm, so it is not 105 cm. 105 cm would be 1,05 m.)

items.q: Convert. 0,7 cm = ☐ mm
items.e: 1 cm = 10 mm. Centimetres are bigger than millimetres, so multiply by 10: 0,7 × 10 = 7. The digits move 1 place to the left. So 0,7 cm = 7 mm.

items.q: Convert. 65 cm = ☐ m
items.e: 1 m = 100 cm. Centimetres are smaller than metres, so divide by 100: 65 ÷ 100 = 0,65. The digits move 2 places to the right. So 65 cm = 0,65 m.

items.q: Convert. 75 m = ☐ km
items.e: 1 km = 1 000 m. Metres are smaller than kilometres, so divide by 1 000: 75 ÷ 1 000 = 0,075. The digits move 3 places to the right. So 75 m = 0,075 km. Check: 0,75 km would be 750 m.

items.q: Convert. 1,08 m = ☐ cm

Which is the same as 0,305 km?
items.e: Multiply by 1 000: 0,305 × 1 000 = 305 m. The 0 holds the tenths place, so it is not 35 m.

items.q: Which is the longest?
items.e: Change them all to metres: 0,5 km = 500 m, 5 200 cm = 52 m and 0,48 km = 480 m. 500 m is the longest. 5 200 cm has the biggest number, but centimetres are small.

items.q: Which is the shortest?
items.e: Change them all to millimetres: 6,5 cm = 65 mm, 0,07 m = 70 mm and 0,6 m = 600 mm. 65 mm is the shortest.

items.q: Which is true?
items.e: 1,2 × 1 000 = 1 200, so 1,2 km = 1 200 m. The others are wrong: 0,3 m = 30 cm, 45 mm = 0,045 m and 2,5 m = 2 500 mm.

items.q: Which list goes from the shortest to the longest?
items.e: Change them all to metres: 0,09 km = 90 m and 9 600 cm = 96 m. 90 < 95 < 96.

items.q: Put these in order from shortest to longest: 1,2 m, 125 cm, 1 150 mm, 0,13 km
items.e: Change them all to centimetres: 1,2 m = 120 cm, 1 150 mm = 115 cm and 0,13 km = 130 m = 13 000 cm. 115 < 120 < 125 < 13 000. (0,13 km has the smallest number but is by far the longest.)

items.e: Use one unit: 1,5 m = 150 cm. 150 − 105 = 45 cm. (1 395 cm treats 1,5 m as 1 500 cm, and 0,45 cm puts the wrong unit on 0,45 m.)
